sections.heading: Execution Payload Bid Gossip
sections.summary: Two competing PRs for bid gossip validation reviewed; decision deferred a few days for more client review.
sections.body:
- Two PRs address a bug where a builder sends a high bid to the network but a low bid directly to the proposer, causing the proposer to accept the worse bid.
  - [PR 5774](https://github.com/ethereum/consensus-specs/pull/5774): Tells the proposer to accept duplicate bids from the same builder regardless of value, but only at the proposer side.
  - [PR 5776](https://github.com/ethereum/consensus-specs/pull/5776) (Nico/Lodestar): Allows builders to submit increasingly valuable bids with a 3% minimum increment and 0.001 ETH floor, enabling staged bidding from a single index without needing multiple builder indices.
- Justin Traglia prefers Nico's PR; at ~0.5 ETH final value the 3% increment limits a builder to ~200 bids per slot.
- Potuz (Prysm) expressed discomfort with over-specifying this topic: the proposer should accept any bid regardless, so the fix is purely proposer-side; adding network-level caches and increment checks adds unnecessary complexity. Prysm would likely not implement the more complex version.
- Barnabas asked whether the 3% threshold could be a client implementation detail rather than spec; Justin explained builders need a consistent spec across clients to know the increment.
- Enrico (Teku) noted a side effect: if clients implement custom filtering, reference tests for gossip validation could conflict with production behavior.
- Decision deferred: Justin requested a few more days for client review before merging either PR. ACDT next week is canceled (Devcon), so resolution expected async in the coming days.
- Separately, [PR 5770](https://github.com/ethereum/consensus-specs/pull/5770) adds missing checks from fork choice into execution payload gossip validation to prevent invalid payloads from being gossiped.
  - Prysm confirmed support; Teku already independently implemented the block hash check.
  - PR believed ready to merge; a few more client plus-ones requested before merging.

sections.heading: Glamsterdam Rollout and Devnet Planning
sections.summary: A new consensus-specs release planned for tomorrow; Glamsterdam devnet targeting mid-November at earliest.
sections.body:
- Barnabas raised the question of rollout timelines given pending consensus changes including a consensus-breaking Lido PR.
- Justin Traglia plans a consensus-specs release approximately tomorrow (next day).
- Client implementations before Devcon considered unlikely; earliest devnet launch estimated around November 16–20.
- Potuz suggested Kurtosis testing may be more appropriate than a full devnet for certain changes (e.g., deposit onboarding at the fork).
- stokes noted that with Hoodi's timeline uncertain, there is some slack, but changes should not linger indefinitely.

sections.heading: EIP-8015 SFI
sections.summary: EIP-8015 (Beacon state cleanup) moved from CFI to SFI with no opposition.
sections.body:
- [EIP-8015](https://eips.ethereum.org/EIPS/eip-8015) is already merged into the Heze spec and has been tested on devnets.
- Barnabas proposed SFI immediately; Potuz, Lighthouse, Teku, Lodestar, ethrex, and multiple others expressed support.
- No objections raised.
- Decision: EIP-8015 moved to SFI.

sections.heading: EIP-8365 (0x00 Deposit Deprecation)
sections.summary: Decision deferred to next call on whether to burn ETH or use an activation gate for post-fork 0x00 deposits.
sections.body:
- [EIP-8365](https://eips.ethereum.org/EIPS/eip-8365) removes the ability to create new 0x00 validators; the open question is what happens to ETH deposited via 0x00 after the fork.
- Barnabas proposed an alternative to NC's original design: instead of burning ETH, the validator's balance is zeroed and re-entered into the pending deposit queue, requiring reactivation as a 0x01 validator via BLS-to-execution change.
  - This prevents an attack vector where large amounts of dormant 0x00 stake could become active in a single epoch.
- Potuz acknowledged the proposal but noted it is simpler to just drop the deposit and burn the ETH.
- NC argued for keeping the protocol simple since 0x00 deposits are rare.
- Barnabas outlined a multi-fork deprecation roadmap: stop new 0x00 validators in Hegota, exit remaining 0x00 validators in a subsequent fork, remove BLS-to-execution change entirely after that.
- Kevaundray Wedderburn asked whether existing 0x00 depositors before the fork would still be accepted (yes, only post-fork deposits affected).
- Barnabas noted that tools like ethdo still support 0x00 deposits, so users may not see announcements.
- NC requested this be settled definitively at the next discussion, noting it has been raised on multiple calls.
- Decision deferred to next ACDC call (2 weeks), with in-person conversations at Devcon expected to help converge.
- Two open PRs: [EIP PR 12513](https://github.com/ethereum/EIPs/pull/12513) and [EIP PR 12533](https://github.com/ethereum/EIPs/pull/12533).

sections.heading: FOCIL Clarification for EL Rebuild Behavior
sections.summary: Barnabas flagged that ELs rebuild blocks from scratch when inclusion list arrives; needs EL input, deferred to next ACD.
sections.body:
- Barnabas observed on devnet 3 that when inclusion list transactions arrive, some EL clients drop their existing payload and regenerate from scratch at ~6 seconds into the slot, causing missed blocks.
- His proposal: if payload attributes already exist, the inclusion list should append transactions rather than trigger a full block rebuild.
- NC noted this likely needs EL team input; from CL perspective it seems fine.
- Toni Wahrstätter commented in chat that it is not trivial on the EL side: post-execution system calls (e.g., withdrawals) mean the appended transactions must be inserted before withdrawal processing, requiring the EL to checkpoint state.
- Decision: topic deferred to the next ACD-EL call for EL team discussion.

sections.heading: EIP-8334: Bundled Attestation Propagation (CFI)
sections.summary: EIP-8334 CFI'd after simulation showed ~50% attestation bandwidth reduction; networking-only change laying groundwork for decoupled consensus.
sections.body:
- Sukun Tarachandani presented simulation results from a cloud devnet testing decoupled consensus (targeted for ISTAR).
  - Simulated mainnet-equivalent load: single subnet with 2,000+ validators, split between home nodes and super nodes.
  - Without EIP-8334: home node outbound bandwidth exceeded 25 Mbps, reaching ~40 Mbps, choking outbound capacity and interfering with goldfish votes.
  - With EIP-8334 (bundling attestations with signatures, even bundles of 4): bandwidth reduced by approximately half (~20 Mbps outbound, ~10 Mbps inbound).
- The EIP bundles attestation data with signatures instead of repeating attestation data for each individual attestation, reducing redundancy.
- Implementation details: purely a networking change (~500 LOC in Lighthouse, ~700 LOC in Prysm), does not affect state transition or attestation data structure itself; only the outer network object changes.
  - Consensus-specs PR: [PR 5464](https://github.com/ethereum/consensus-specs/pull/5464)
- Sukun noted the EIP has been modified to also work over Waggle (a new networking system), and is backwards compatible / does not need fork alignment.
- Potuz raised concern about fork transition: during the first slots after activation, nodes must handle both old and new attestation formats.
  - Barnabas suggested subscribing to both topics two epochs before and one epoch after the transition.
- Nico (Lodestar) questioned whether it's worth touching attestation structures before decoupled consensus; Sukun clarified attestation data itself is unchanged.
- Lighthouse, Prysm, and Teku expressed support; Grandine suggested revisiting later if time permits.
- Potuz noted attestation bandwidth is "probably the most important topic to tackle in the next few years."
- Decision: EIP-8334 moved to CFI.

sections.heading: EIP-8383: Reduce CL Block Retention Window (CFI)
sections.summary: EIP-8383 CFI'd as a single config value change reducing the retention window; exact value to be revisited.
sections.body:
- [EIP-8383](https://github.com/ethereum/execution-specs/issues/3667) reduces the CL block retention window by changing a single configuration parameter.
- Kevaundray Wedderburn (champion) confirmed it is ready for consideration; the value change cascades to history expiry, blob retention window, etc., as these were already aligned in Glamsterdam.
- The proposed value is 8192, aligning with Toni's state-diff retention EIP ([EIP-8252](https://eips.ethereum.org/EIPS/eip-8252)).
- Lighthouse said CFI; Lodestar and Teku expressed support in chat; Nico noted the exact value should be revisited.
- No opposition raised.
- Decision: EIP-8383 moved to CFI.

sections.heading: EIP-8205: Withdrawal Credentials Preregistration (DFI)
sections.summary: EIP-8205 DFI'd; core devs committed to solving deposit front-running with PQ deposit contract redesign instead.
sections.body:
- Dima (Lido) proposed CFI for EIP-8205 to address the deposit front-running vulnerability, arguing it should remain CFI as a backstop until PQ designs are confirmed to solve the issue.
- Kevaundray Wedderburn noted that neither of the two current PQ deposit contract proposals (EIP-8413 splitting staker/operator, and the current-design variant) actually solves the front-running issue; one only disincentivizes it.
- Potuz argued the fix should come with PQ since the deposit flow will change anyway, and introducing EIP-8205 now would constrain PQ design unnecessarily. He stated: "If we agree that this has to be solved, and anyways we are going to have to change the deposit flow, then PQ is the optimal place to do this."
- Greg K (Lido) emphasized the risk that DFI means the issue never gets solved, and asked for at least a consensus commitment that it will be addressed in PQ.
- Lighthouse said DFI but would not block inclusion if other clients strongly favor it; Teku confirmed support for the EIP.
- Nico (Lodestar) expressed that protocol should not solve problems handleable off-chain; Enrico (Teku) countered that it is a protocol flaw.
- Decision: EIP-8205 moved to DFI, with a strong call-out that deposit front-running must be resolved as part of the PQ deposit contract design. Potuz stated PQ designers should not be bound to the current deposit design at all.

sections.heading: EIP-8148: Custom Sweep Threshold for Validators (CFI)
sections.summary: EIP-8148 CFI'd; allows validators to set custom sweep thresholds between 32 and 2048 ETH, encouraging consolidation.
sections.body:
- Dima (Lido) presented EIP-8148: allows validators to set a custom sweep threshold (any value between 32 and 2048 ETH) at creation or reconfigure it later via an EL system contract similar to EIP-7002/7251.
  - Eliminates the binary choice between Type 1 (32 ETH sweep) and Type 2 (2048 ETH sweep) validators.
  - Expected benefits: 3–10% more of Ethereum stake consolidated in near term; single withdrawal credential type; reduced withdrawal queue pressure; path to deprecating Type 1 validators.
  - Consensus specs already merged into feature folder; spec tests pending CFI; system contract code ready; Lido will fund audit.
  - Working proof of concept in Prysm + Geth + Dora by Manu ([PR link](https://github.com/OffchainLabs/prysm/pull/17338)).
  - Specs: [consensus-specs feature branch](https://github.com/ethereum/consensus-specs/tree/master/specs/_features/eip8148)
- Manu confirmed implementation is low complexity and straightforward on the CL side.
- Independent security researchers reviewed and found no major issues.
- Lighthouse indicated DFI initially but would not block if others are strongly in favor; updated to support given other clients' backing.
- Teku: "Worth moving forward."
- Potuz trusted Manu's assessment that implementation was safe and easy; wanted to see benchmarks on the sweep loop impact.
- Decision: EIP-8148 moved to CFI.

sections.heading: EIP-8411: Fast Execution Payload Broadcast (CFI)
sections.summary: EIP-8411 CFI'd; chunks large payloads into shards for faster P2P propagation, showing ~3x improvement in simulations.
sections.body:
- Kamil Salakhiev presented EIP-8411: replaces naive full-message gossipsub forwarding with chunked shard propagation for large execution payloads.
  - Current gossipsub requires downloading the full message before forwarding, causing severe slowdowns for large payloads.
  - Simulations with 4,000 nodes using EIP-7870 showed ~3x propagation speed improvement even with pessimistic assumptions about slow nodes.
  - Increasingly important given gas limit increases in Glamsterdam and potential slot duration decreases.
- Prysm strongly in favor (Potuz called for SFI); Lighthouse, Teku, ethrex, Grandine, and multiple others expressed CFI support.
- Lighthouse noted their main objection had been gossipsub-related but they would not block.
- Daniel Knopik estimated ~500 LOC for Lighthouse, networking-only.
- Decision: EIP-8411 moved to CFI.

sections.heading: Moderator Transition
sections.summary: stokes stepping down as ACDC moderator; Ben Edgington takes over as lead moderator with Will Corcoran as deputy, starting next call.
sections.body:
- stokes announced he is stepping down as ACDC moderator effective after this call.
- Ben Edgington will serve as lead moderator; Will Corcoran as deputy moderator starting with the next call in 2 weeks.
- Ben Edgington thanked stokes for completing the Hegota scoping before the handoff and expressed enthusiasm for the role.
- Multiple participants thanked stokes for his service.
